items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: they had heard about me so they called Marshall and I met him in Palestine, Texas, and we played a job there that night.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Well, uh, I'm getting a little out of order with my questions. Uh, we can jump around. And someday Johnny will edit this. When he, when he follows in my footsteps. We'll have him do all the dirty work. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh, where did, uh, Ham Crawford work, you say, in the, in all, that through the West?

Ham Crawford, uh, was a well-known name. And, uh, we talked about him before. Ham was a, a really fine saxophonist and, uh, played the clarinet. Played an E-flat clarinet, which he was a trickster with. He, uh, he's taught me how to break the clarinet in two and play on the upper, uh, section of the clarinet and juggle the other part and throw it on the legs. He was a real clown with a clarinet. Yes. This was, uh, part of the job in the twenties was, uh, getting over, selling, uh, herself in that respect. Ham was…
